extracted.intended_audience: Commission officials preparing new initiatives, managing existing policies, and managers responsible for quality control and allocation of resources
extracted.subtask_description: Operational internal guidelines for Commission staff on designing, assessing and implementing EU policy and legislation across the policy cycle (planning, consultation, impact assessment, evaluation, implementation and monitoring).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'better regulation'
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Better regulation' is about creating legislation that achieves its objectives while being targeted, effective, easy to comply with and with the least burden possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is a way of working to prepare political decisions in an open, transparent and evidence-informed manner; not about regulating or deregulating per se. It should ensure subsidiarity and proportionality and aim for broad public support, fitness for purpose and future-proofing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comprehensive approach
rubrics_metrics.description: Considerations should cover all relevant economic, social and environmental impacts, all interested parties and every phase in the policy cycle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In particular any significant impacts on gender equality, territorial and rural issues, geopolitical context, external implications, competitiveness and SMEs must be transparently assessed and presented; impacts on third countries should also be considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coherent approach
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure consistency with high-level and long-term policy objectives and across EU laws and regulation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply principles such as 'do no significant harm' and 'digital by default', implement European Climate Law objectives, mainstream SDGs and strategic foresight to check policy consistency and avoid isolated or contradictory measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proportionate approach
rubrics_metrics.description: The approach should be proportionate to the expected impacts and focus analysis where it matters most.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Depth of analysis should reflect the significance of impacts; apply common sense and proportionality rather than procedural box-ticking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participative approach
rubrics_metrics.description: All interested parties (experts, individuals, groups affected) should be able to contribute to policymaking by expressing views and providing data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult broadly and inclusively, making consultations progressively accessible to persons with disabilities and avoiding consultation fatigue by targeting appropriately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence-based approach
rubrics_metrics.description: Policy decisions need to be informed by the best available evidence (including scientific evidence where available).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evidence can be quantitative or qualitative, including statistics, stakeholder input, evaluations and expert advice; use data.europa.eu and Tool #4 for operational guidance on evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency
rubrics_metrics.description: Prepare laws and regulation in a transparent way by documenting the process, making evidence available and explaining the underlying rationale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publish consultation documents, contributions and results (e.g., on 'Have Your Say'), and explain how stakeholder input was taken into account to improve legitimacy and accountability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Learning from experience / 'evaluate first' principle
rubrics_metrics.description: Policymakers need to learn from implementation experience; the 'evaluate first' principle should apply whenever legislation is revised.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use evaluations and fitness checks to identify whether legislation remains fit for purpose, requires adjustment or should be repealed; systematically monitor implementation to enable meaningful future evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forward planning and political validation
rubrics_metrics.description: Political validation at the appropriate level is required before substantive work on an initiative can start and stakeholders can be consulted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A valid entry in Decide is required; political validation is a green light for preparatory work but does not prejudge final outcomes. Allow time for RSB scrutiny, interservice consultation and translation as part of planning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stakeholder consultation as essential
rubrics_metrics.description: Stakeholder consultation is an essential element of policy preparation and review and supports evaluations, impact assessments and preparation of initiatives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan consultations with a concise strategy to identify and target relevant stakeholders and gather all relevant evidence. Consult as widely as possible while avoiding consultation fatigue and provide feedback to respondents on use of contributions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Call for evidence / Have Your Say entry point
rubrics_metrics.description: The consultation system is based on the 'call for evidence' published on the 'Have Your Say' web portal which is the single entry point for contributions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The 'call for evidence' combines feedback documents (translated into all EU languages) and, when required, a public consultation. Use this portal as the primary publication channel for public consultations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope and exclusions of stakeholder consultation
rubrics_metrics.description: Stakeholder consultation covers public and targeted consultations in preparing policy initiatives or evaluating interventions, but excludes interinstitutional consultations, certain expert-group opinions, consultations by EU agencies prior to Commission finalisation of delegated/implementing acts, and citizens' initiatives under Article 11(4) TEU.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also does not replace treaty or legislative consultation frameworks (e.g., consultative committees, social partner consultations) and applies without prejudice to environmental consultation requirements (Regulation 1367/2006).

rubrics_metrics.name: General principles for consultation
rubrics_metrics.description: Four general principles govern relations with stakeholders: participation, openness and accountability, effectiveness, and coherence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Participation = inclusive approach; Openness/accountability = make process and its effect transparent; Effectiveness = consult when views can still influence outcomes; Coherence = consistent processes and quality control across services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum standards for consultation: clarity
rubrics_metrics.description: All consultation documents should be clear and concise and include all necessary information to facilitate responses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technical questionnaires should include a set of general questions for non-specialists to improve accessibility and usefulness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum standards for consultation: targeting
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure the consultation strategy targets all interested parties so they have an opportunity to express their opinions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify relevant stakeholders and use targeted activities to gather evidence; take account of different territories and groups (urban/rural, outermost regions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum standards for consultation: outreach
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure adequate awareness-raising and publicity and adapt communication channels to target audiences; publish public consultations on 'Have Your Say'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a range of communication tools and adapt channels for accessibility (including persons with disabilities).

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum standards for consultation: sufficient time
rubrics_metrics.description: Allow sufficient time for planning and responses; as a rule, 'calls for evidence' including public consultations are published for 12 weeks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions may apply in emergencies or where rapid action is necessary, but timing should generally permit meaningful participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum standards for consultation: publication of contributions and results
rubrics_metrics.description: Publish public consultation contributions and results on 'Have Your Say' and, where possible, on DG websites with links.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a synopsis report explaining how contributions were used as part of the impact assessment or evaluation documentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: When stakeholder consultation is required
rubrics_metrics.description: Consultation (call for evidence and, where required, public consultation) is required for impact assessments, evaluations of broad public interest and fitness checks, and generally before preparing initiatives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certain short or technical initiatives may be exempt; political validation is needed before consultations start. See Chapter II and toolbox for detailed triggers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation objective criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluations gather evidence to assess how a specific intervention has performed against earlier expectations, including whether there were unintended effects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluations should conclude whether the intervention remains fit for purpose, should be adjusted for effectiveness/relevance/coherence or should be repealed, and draw on monitoring data and stakeholder input.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fitness check definition and purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: A fitness check is a comprehensive evaluation of a policy area assessing how a set of related legislative acts contributed to policy objectives (or horizontal issues across many acts).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fitness checks identify overlaps, inconsistencies, synergies, digitalisation potential and cumulative impacts; they are suited to assessing regulatory burdens and simplification potential.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impact assessment core requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Impact assessments must (1) identify and describe the problem to be tackled, (2) establish objectives for EU action, (3) formulate policy options, assess their potential impacts and where appropriate identify a preferred option, and (4) set out how expected results will be monitored and evaluated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: They follow an integrated approach assessing environmental, social and economic impacts and should mainstream sustainability and SDGs into policymaking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quantification and proportionality of impacts
rubrics_metrics.description: Where feasible and proportionate, the Commission should quantify impacts including costs and benefits, although it is not always possible across diverse policy areas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quantify compliance costs where feasible; administrative burdens are subject to offsetting under 'one in, one out'. Provide justified estimates in analytical reports if a full impact assessment cannot be produced.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of specific impact categories
rubrics_metrics.description: Impact assessments and reports must include description of social, economic and environmental impacts and explicit statements if any are not considered significant; indicate who will be affected and quantify costs/benefits where possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Special attention to impacts on fundamental rights, SMEs and competitiveness; consideration of 'do no significant harm', 'digital by default', European Climate Law conformity and assessment of relevant SDGs; include consultation strategy and synopsis report.

rubrics_metrics.name: RSB quality control and opinion types
rubrics_metrics.description: The Regulatory Scrutiny Board (RSB) assesses impact assessments, fitness checks and selected evaluations and issues opinions: for impact assessments - positive, positive with reservations, negative; for evaluations/fitness checks - positive or negative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A positive RSB opinion is needed before interservice consultation for initiatives supported by impact assessments. DGs must address RSB recommendations; negative opinions require resubmission after amendment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report structure and length guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Impact assessment main report should be limited to 40 pages of text with technical annexes as appropriate; executive summary 4-5 DGT pages as a separate linked SWD translated into all EU languages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write with non-expert readers in mind; ensure clarity on problem, EU action appropriateness, pros/cons of options and affected parties; balance main text and annexes and systematically reference external material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explanatory memorandum content requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The explanatory memorandum accompanying proposals should cover legal basis, subsidiarity, proportionality, results of evaluations/fitness checks, stakeholder consultation results, summary of external expert input, impact assessment process (or justification if none), RSB consultation, regulatory fitness and simplification, conformity with Charter of Fundamental Rights, main impact categories, 'do no significant harm' and 'digital by default' conformity, SDG contributions, and monitoring/evaluation arrangements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The explanatory memorandum is transmitted to other institutions and made public but not published in the Official Journal and does not form part of the adopted act; use templates in Tool #40 where relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implementation strategy content
rubrics_metrics.description: An implementation strategy should identify potential implementation problems, the types of support the Commission will provide to assist Member States in transposition and implementation, and set out arrangements for monitoring implementation including timelines for compliance assessments and possible enforcement action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare strategies for all major directives and regulations unless limited scope, built-in tracking, or minimal obligations apply; include interservice consultation alongside impact assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoidance of 'gold-plating' and reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: When transposing directives Member States should refrain from unjustified 'gold-plating' (going beyond directive requirements) and ensure a level playing field; Member States must provide precise accounts of how national provisions transpose directive obligations and may indicate where they go beyond requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commission will report annually on monitoring application of EU law and instances of gold-plating and encourage publication of national transposition texts on EUR-Lex.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance promotion tools and use
rubrics_metrics.description: Compliance promotion tools (guidance documents, expert groups, explanatory documents, training, workshops, package meetings) should be used regularly to prevent or correct breaches and avoid infringement proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose a combination of tools adapted to policy area, legal instrument type and national systems, taking into account resource constraints and potential burden on Member States.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitoring principles
rubrics_metrics.description: A well-designed monitoring system should be governed by comprehensiveness, proportionality, minimal overlap, timeliness and accessibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monitoring should cover all objectives, reflect data collection costs, avoid duplication by focussing on data gaps, ensure evidence is ready for planned evaluations, and make evidence publicly available with clear confidentiality/data protection arrangements where needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Key monitoring questions
rubrics_metrics.description: Monitoring systems must address: (1) what evidence should be collected; (2) when and how evidence should be collected; and (3) who will collect the evidence and from whom.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Link objectives and indicators carefully, consider timing and existing data, assign responsibilities for collection, and bear in mind cumulative burdens on data providers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality control responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Quality control of better regulation processes starts in DGs, with Secretariat-General providing methodological guidance and the RSB as central independent quality control for certain outputs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DGs must present results in SWDs for RSB review; interservice groups contribute expertise; Secretariat-General monitors application of guidelines and can propose burden-elimination measures in consultation with the better regulation network.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application with proportionality and exemptions
rubrics_metrics.description: The guidelines and toolbox should be applied in a proportionate manner using common sense and exemptions can be requested in cases such as emergencies, political imperatives or confidentiality needs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exemption requests should be made at political validation via Decide or to the better regulation unit (functional mailbox) for cases arising after validation; external communication of approach and justification is required (typically via the 'call for evidence').

rubrics_metrics.name: 'One in, one out' and burden offsetting
rubrics_metrics.description: For initiatives with significant cost implications, analyze and quantify compliance costs where feasible; administrative burdens are subject to offsetting under the 'one in, one out' approach.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Impact assessments should present estimates of adjustment and administrative costs; where a full IA cannot be produced, justified cost estimates should appear in analytical reports within 3 months. Use the dedicated online administrative burden calculator and report within appropriate remit (DG, REFIT area or broader policy area). Flexibilities include intra-period flexibility, trading across policy areas and exemptions in exceptional circumstances.
